assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental and theoretical demonstration that electrons tunnel over long distances through folded proteins, with rates controlled by distance and the intervening medium. This is the physical principle behind respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer; it is a mechanism stated in physical terms and tested with time-resolved kinetics on engineered redox proteins, which is the kind of result I value most.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear core pair, with a long, consistent joint program of ruthenium-modified proteins and flash-quench kinetics. The credited set is only two people, so the three-laureate limit is not a problem. Wider field credit to others such as Marcus-theory developers (already recognised in 1992) and to Beratan/Onuchic tunneling-pathway theory is outside the supplied credit and would need care in the citation.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent confirmation and incorporation into textbook bioenergetics; interpretation stable. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery or as an extension of Marcus electron-transfer theory already prized.
Details of tunneling-pathway versus averaged-medium models remain debated; I am relying on memory, not verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and the FeMo cofactor with interstitial carbide, followed by trapping of substrate-bound and CO-bound states, opened a mechanistic account of biological N2 reduction, one of the most demanding enzyme reactions in chemistry. It combines structure, spectroscopy and kinetics around a fundamental electron/proton-coupled problem.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the early structures and cofactor chemistry; Einsle contributed the central carbide and high-resolution structures; Seefeldt contributed the kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism (Lowe-Thorneley framework). Dean and Ribbe are credible alternatives, so the three-name selection involves a real priority judgment and could be contested.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism, where N2 binds and how the E4 state works, is still actively debated and not settled. Recognition is mature for structure and less so for mechanism.
uncertainties: Unresolved substrate binding site and catalytic intermediates.
Competing credit for biochemical and genetic work (Dean, Ribbe, Burgess, Hoffman) that cannot all fit in three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that liquid-liquid phase separation can organise cellular contents without membranes and so reframed how intracellular chemistry is compartmentalised. The concept is physical, widely generative and has transformed cell biology, though the field is young and its molecular-level chemistry is still being developed.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne published the foundational P granule work (2009) and Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction biochemical basis (2012). That is a plausible three, with Pappu and Mittag contributing physical chemistry theory and sequence grammar that would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption but substantial ongoing debate about which cellular condensates are truly liquid-like and functional in vivo, and about artefacts of overexpression. Possibly premature as a chemistry prize.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of many condensates is still controversial.
Whether the committee regards this as chemistry rather than cell biology or physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography with XFEL pulses enabled diffraction-before-destruction, room-temperature structures from micro-crystals, and time-resolved molecular movies of enzyme reactions and photoreceptors. It is a method that made dynamic mechanisms visible, which is directly in line with my interest in combining time-resolved spectroscopy and structure.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle with Fromme, Hajdu and others, while Hajdu originated the diffraction-before-destruction concept and is a key priority claim. Schlichting is central for the time-resolved chemistry. Choosing three of four involves an unavoidable and contestable priority judgement; I would weigh Hajdu's conceptual role against Fromme's.
assessment.maturity: The method is well confirmed and widely adopted at several facilities. Time-resolved chemical results are still accumulating, so the lasting scientific impact is partly ahead of us.
uncertainties: Hajdu versus Fromme for the third place; Hajdu's death or current status I am not able to confirm.
Share of impact compared with synchrotron serial methods, which grew out of the XFEL work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central concept in respiratory enzymes, photosystem II and catalysis. The theory of concerted and sequential PCET and the associated bond-weakening thermochemistry give physical language for exactly the processes I work on. It is of fundamental chemical significance, though much of the field is conceptual refinement.
assessment.attribution: Hammes-Schiffer supplied the vibronic theory, Mayer the thermochemical and mechanistic framework, and Nocera the model-system and catalysis demonstrations. Meyer is the pioneer of the concept in inorganic systems and so there is a real priority question; I also note my own field proximity, which I should declare when judging.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and in widespread use, but the field is diffuse, and the credit is distributed across many groups, so a single clearly attributable discovery is harder to identify.
uncertainties: Whether this rests on a line of work rather than a single attributable discovery.
Meyer's early role versus the three selected.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiencies from a few percent to over 25 percent within a decade, using solution-processed materials. It is of great practical and materials importance, with a rich defect and ion-migration chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009); Park and Gratzel produced the solid-state 2012 device, and Snaith's 2012 meso-superstructured cell triggered the explosive growth. Kanatzidis, Seok and Gratzel are also credible, so choosing three is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently confirmed, but long-term stability and toxicity are unresolved, which argues that recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead content could weaken the case at this time.
Allocation between Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Gratzel.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation-based methods (TROSY, relaxation dispersion) allow atomic-resolution study of the structure and dynamics of large proteins and their excited states, giving direct access to the motions that underlie function. NMR structure determination was prized in 2002, so the case rests on later and distinct advances.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay all made clearly identified methodological contributions: triple resonance and residual dipolar couplings, and dynamics and invisible states. Wagner and Palmer are plausible alternatives; the claim of distinctness from Wuthrich's 2002 prize needs to be evaluated.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and thoroughly confirmed; widely adopted. Recognition is timely or even late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Nobel Prize for NMR of biomolecules.
Which of the several close contributors to include.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnel-shaped energy landscape and the principle of minimal frustration resolved Levinthal's paradox and give a physical statistical-mechanical basis for protein folding, which later fed into structure prediction. It is conceptually deep, but a theory prize needs experimental anchoring.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson developed the landscape formalism, Dill the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model view, and Fersht the experimental phi-value analysis. Fersht as an experimentalist is an obvious part of any well-balanced citation, but the selection is mine to make from the list, so I keep to the theory core and note the credit is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Concept is long established and widely accepted. The 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design has partly overtaken the theme, which could reduce or increase the case for recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize for AlphaFold and Rosetta.
Whether a theory-led prize without Fersht gives a balanced attribution.
